# Renewable Energy Outlook 2023

This note summarises where renewable power stands and what is driving it. The figures below come from public reports.

## Investment and costs

Global investment in renewable energy reached $500 billion in 2022.[1] Solar module prices fell 89% between 2010 and 2020 [2]. Heat pumps outsold gas furnaces in the United States in 2022 [2].

## Capacity

Offshore wind capacity in Europe grew from 11 GW in 2015 to 25 GW in 2020 [3]. Battery storage additions doubled in 2021, e.g. in grid-scale projects [4]. Utility-scale hydrogen projects reached 3.5 GW of announced capacity by 2022 [5]. According to [the IRENA capacity statistics](https://example.net/irena-capacity), solar PV capacity passed 1,000 GW worldwide in 2022.

## Jobs and prices

Employment in the solar industry grew faster than in fossil fuels (Chen et al., 2020). Solar was the cheapest source of new electricity in most markets by 2020 [1–2].

The authors expect these trends to continue.

## References

[1] Smith, J., & Lee, K. (2021). "Global renewable investment trends." Energy Journal. https://example.org/energy-journal/investment-trends
[2] International Energy Agency. (2021). "Solar PV module price trends." doi:10.5555/iea.solar.2021
[3] "Offshore wind in Europe: 2020 statistics," WindEurope, 2021.
[4] Okafor, N. (2022). "Battery storage additions in 2021." Storage Digest. https://example.com/old-report
[5] Garcia, M. (2022). "Hydrogen project pipeline review." H2 Quarterly. https://example.org/h2-pipeline
[6] Chen, L., Ortiz, M., & Patel, R. (2020). "Jobs in the energy transition." Labor Economics Review. https://example.edu/jobs-energy-transition
